tea.title: The radiator in 6C
tea.question: What did Mrs. Kessler ask about that afternoon?
hints: Mrs. Kessler is at home in 6C from half past four to half past five.
Knock at 6C. The radiator is your reason to be there.
Speak to Mrs. Kessler about her radiator, and mind what she asks in return.

friday.title: Friday's errand
friday.question: Who went up to the sixth floor that evening, and carrying what?
hints: Two people in this house went up that evening. One lives in 4C, one in 3A.
Knock at 4C for Cam Ortiz, and at 3A for Malcolm Reed. Be done by nine.
Ask Cam what went to 6C that Friday. Ask Malcolm about the evening upstairs.

yard.title: The stairs before light
yard.question: Who was already awake?
hints: Someone on the first floor is already awake.
Knock at 1D. Teresa Vale has not slept.
Let Teresa Vale tell you what she heard from the stairs. You have little more than half an hour.

playback.title: The twelfth record
playback.question: What was playing behind the wall?
hints: Cal Dwyer in 5B keeps his recordings.
Knock at 5B in the evening and ask to hear the twelfth.
If he will not play it, something learned elsewhere is wanting. Go home and look to your other leads.

ash.title: The ash pit
ash.question: What did not burn?
hints: The boiler room is Omar Bell's business. He lives in 3B.
Ask Omar Bell what is in the ash pit.
If he has nothing to say, something learned elsewhere is wanting. Go home and look to your other leads.

same_friday.line: The afternoon in June and the errand in July touch the same door.

between_two_witnesses.line: One saw the evening begin. One heard the night end. The hours between belong to nobody.

what_was_arranged.line: A sound that was made to be heard, and a thing that was made to be gone.
